extracted.intended_audience: librarians, faculty, instructors, researchers, and academic students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers, reviewers, and librarians on how peer review works, the types of peer review, preprint posting (Advance), and resources for becoming and conducting peer reviewers in humanities and social sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is "a process where scientists (aka peers) evaluate the quality of other scientists’ work. By doing this, they aim to ensure the work is rigorous, coherent, uses past research and adds to what we already know."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition frames peer review as evaluative (rigour, coherence, use of prior research, and contribution to knowledge). The page points readers to an explainer from Social Science Space for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation (function of peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is an effective form of research evaluation to help select the highest quality articles for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer review to identify and prioritize manuscripts of highest quality for publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity (function of peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review ensures the integrity of the publishing process and the scholarly record. Reviewers are independent of journal publications and the research being conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer independence is emphasised as a core integrity requirement; conflicts of interest should be avoided so the scholarly record remains trustworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality improvement (function of peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filtering process and revision advice improve the quality of the final research article as well as offering the author new insights into their research methods and the results that they have compiled. Peer review gives authors access to the opinions of experts in the field who can provide support and insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should provide constructive revision advice to improve methodology, interpretation, and presentation; peer review is not just gatekeeping but developmental feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-anonymized peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-anonymized – the name of the reviewer is hidden from the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common journal policy: reviewers remain anonymous to authors; check journal-specific submission guidelines for implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-anonymized peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-anonymized – names are hidden from both reviewers and the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reduce bias by concealing identities; verify how a specific journal operationalizes anonymization (e.g., manuscript redaction requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Triple-anonymized peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Triple-anonymized – names are hidden from authors, reviewers, and the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stricter anonymization that also conceals identities from editors; may have procedural implications for handling submissions and editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open / Transparent peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review comes in many forms. At Sage we offer a form of open peer review on four journals via our Transparent Peer Review program, whereby the reviews are published alongside the article. The names of the reviewers may also be published, depending on the reviewers’ preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open/transparent review can include publishing review reports and optionally reviewer names; policies vary by journal and reviewer consent is often sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Post publication peer review can offer useful interaction and a discussion forum for the research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-publication review provides ongoing discussion and feedback but is not usual or appropriate in all fields; suitability depends on disciplinary norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check manuscript submission guidelines for review method
rubrics_metrics.description: Please double check the manuscript submission guidelines of the journal you are reviewing in order to ensure that you understand the method of peer review being used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A procedural requirement: before reviewing, confirm the journal's chosen peer review model and any reviewer instructions or policies (e.g., anonymization, confidentiality, conflicts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance preprints: eligible types and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance allows researchers within the fields of humanities and social sciences to post their work online and free of charge. Advance welcomes a variety of preprint types, including, but not limited to, original research, literature reviews, commentaries, and case studies. Once accepted, each preprint will be freely available online to the research community and peers and will benefit from our monitored commenting feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprints should adhere to the platform's submission guidelines; authors should expect monitored community feedback and public availability. Check Advance submission guidelines for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: 7 Benefits of Preprints (PDF file) — Learn more about the benefits of preprints using this infographic you can download and share with others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit guidance: preprints increase visibility and enable early feedback; authors and reviewers can use preprints to solicit community input prior to formal publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer training and ethics resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage Peer Review Support Resources — Sage Journal Reviewer Gateway; Guide to Becoming a Peer Reviewer; Video: How to Become a Peer Reviewer; Video: How to Conduct Peer Review; Video: Peer Review Ethics; Infographic: Your Paper and Peer Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these resources for reviewer development: learn how to perform reviews, understand ethical obligations, and follow best practices. The presence of these resources implies expectations for reviewer competence and ethical conduct.
